opening_message:
Ticket 1: Timothy Wallace (employee ID E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E022.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer. He requested admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so as a full-time employee without ownership, his maximum is write. Admin is above the maximum, so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a contractor with basic security training per the Security DB. Contractors with basic training max out at read (write requires advanced training; admin is never allowed). He requested admin to Payroll, which is above the max, so I recommend granting read.
reason: The request is for admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role; Timothy is an Engineer, so admin is not permitted. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR says full-time (max write) while Security says contractor with basic training (max read; write requires advanced training, admin never allowed). Given conflicting evidence, the conservative, least-privilege decision is read, which is at or below the maximum under either interpretation and does not overgrant.
